venture.hypothesis: If we help independent P&C agencies turn renewal season into a repeatable, agent-approved outreach-and-recommendation workflow by triaging which accounts need action, doing the shopping legwork, and drafting a clear client recommendation, then agencies will retain more at-risk households and convert more renewals into cross-sell or up-sell conversations across their existing book of business, because today that work is too manual and time-consuming for most teams to run account-by-account at scale.

thesis.problem: Every renewal deserves attention most agencies can't consistently give.
thesis.worldAfter: Every renewal reminds customers why their agent matters.
thesis.approach: AI prepares the renewal. The agent owns the client relationship. Upline treats renewal as the agency's most reliable trust-building moment, not just an administrative deadline.

venture.mantra: Make every renewal prove the agent is in my corner.

upcomingProofPoint.description: Members 1st proved agent trust and customer engagement on a real book. Next proof: the same proposal moment with Stockton Hill (Version A outreach). Access is in hand; setup runs Sep 15–16 and the pilot kicks off Friday Sep 18, running three weeks to Oct 9 alongside the MVP build. The strategy sprint (Sep 8–11) closed the plan: percentage-of-premium pricing replaced the flat SaaS fee, seven surfaces sit above the line, and the business intelligence dashboard was cut to an email. A named design partner follows Stockton Hill in October and doubles as the QA population. Path 2 no-AMS ops are in place. MVP launch Nov 6.

pilotSummary.scheduleNote: Members 1st complete. 10 working sessions Jun 17 – Jul 27 + Final Retro Aug 3. Outreach catch-up Jul 20–24. Disposition sheet closed Aug 7: 48 households · 42 emailed · 18 QQ (43%) · 18 recs · 7 switched · 5 stayed · 6 pending. Strategy sprint held Sep 8–11. Stockton Hill access is in hand; account setup Sep 15–16, kickoff Friday Sep 18, three weeks to Oct 9, running alongside the MVP build. Format is Review Fridays — one shopped household walked through together, individual sessions rather than a group.
pilotSummary.clientNamingRule: First name + last initial only (e.g. Daniel P). Never full last names in team-facing exports.

outreachEmail.summary: One boilerplate for every renewal. Only variables: first name, renewal date, new premium (dollars only — no %, no old price, no increase language), and questionnaire link. Premium is never in the first sentence. ~85% rewrite from v1; zero further copy changes after Session 4.
outreachEmail.subject: A quick review of your upcoming renewal
outreachEmail.body:
Hi [First Name],

At Members 1st Insurance, we value you as a member, not just a policyholder. As your renewal on [renewal date] approaches, we'd like to take a few minutes to review your coverage and make sure everything still fits your needs. Sometimes we find our members are missing out on discounts, because over time the information we have no longer reflects your current situation. Your renewal premium for this term is $[new premium].

One of the advantages of working with Members 1st Insurance is that we partner with seven different insurance companies. That means we're able to compare options across multiple carriers to help ensure you're receiving competitive rates and the coverage that's right for you. There's no need to shop your insurance with other carriers when we can do that for you right here. We work on behalf of our members to find the best rates — let us take the guesswork and the multiple phone calls off your plate.

To make sure you're not missing any available discounts or carrying coverage that may no longer match your situation, I've put together a brief questionnaire. Your responses will help us identify potential savings opportunities, verify your current information, and make sure you're properly protected.

[Complete the questionnaire here →]([QUESTIONNAIRE_LINK])

Thank you for being a valued member of Members 1st Insurance. We're committed to helping you protect what matters most while making sure your insurance continues to work for you.

[agent]

recommendationEmail.summary: Post-shop handoff locked short: steer (switch/stay + $) in paragraph one, premium-only recommended-vs-current table at most, coverage reassurance, soft CTA to a call. No jargon, no multi-carrier coverage tables. Agent reviews every quote before client contact. ~60% rewrite from v1.
recommendationEmail.status: Locked at Aug 3 retro — no further template changes. Gerardo S is the canonical short switch example; next design partner resets to Version A.

keyFindings: End-of-pilot funnel (disposition sheet Aug 7): 48 on sheet → 42 emailed → 18 QQ (43%) → 18 recs sent → 7 switched · 5 stayed · 6 pending. Avg savings found ~$474/yr among shopped; ~$665/yr among known switchers.
Outreach collapsed to a single boilerplate (v8, ~85% from v1) — one email for everyone. Held with zero further copy changes through the Aug 3 retro.
Recommendation email locked short (~60% from v1): steer + dollars; depth on the phone. OUTPUT CONTRACT caps length; flag higher deductible; match pay cadence.
Shop threshold held: prioritize ≥15% increases, ranked biggest-first. Preferred product cadence: weekly batch (Mon send / Tue QQ prompts / Fri check), not daily drips.
Upline drafts; agency closes — ~30 min/policy when the client answers (mostly phone). 90–95% quote accuracy with a human double-check is enough; preliminary ≠ bind-ready.
Without the product, proactive disappears — M1 will go reactive during the build pause. Strong intent to adopt day-to-day once built.
Must-haves for day-to-day: EZLynx write-back, weekly batch + QQ notifications, 15%+ priority, short client surfaces, manual mid-term add.
Cross-sell/upsell: 35 households touched; 0 bound by end of pilot — interest surfaces easily; closing is a different motion.
Next design customer resets outreach to Version A — do not inherit Members 1st v8 wording.

notableProgress.note: Canonical short switch: auto to Travelers (~$977 vs Donegal ~$1,630) bundled with Camp Hill home. Agency accepted; email kept short.
Travelers looked ~$665 under until a forgiven at-fault accident hit the report — stayed Donegal. Preliminary ≠ bind-ready.
Switch confirmed with agency corrections (12-mo term, escrow, pay-cadence honesty). Second set of eyes as product requirement.

initiatives.title: Set up the Stockton Hill account
initiatives.notes: Access received. Account setup runs Sep 15–16; the pilot kicks off Friday Sep 18.

initiatives.title: Conduct the Stockton Hill pilot
initiatives.notes: Second design partner. Kickoff Friday Sep 18, three weeks to Oct 9. Format is Review Fridays — one shopped household per session, individual rather than a group. Reset outreach to Version A (do not inherit M1 v8). Runs alongside the MVP build so they react to wireframes while design is still cheap to change. Validate the owner view with Brandon and the CSR view with Stacey.

initiatives.title: Prep the strategy sprint
initiatives.notes: Prep at the open of Labor Day sprint week (Sep 8–11). Stockton Hill is the three weeks after.

initiatives.title: Run the product strategy sprint
initiatives.notes: Complete. Seven sessions Tue–Thu: journeys, magical moments, MVP sketch review, pricing, product breadboard, and the Thursday afternoon close on timeline, lanes and cadence. Outputs are decisions.md, timelines.md and the action tracker. Biggest change of the week was pricing — flat SaaS fee replaced by a percentage of personal-lines premium.

initiatives.title: Plan the MVP
initiatives.notes: Thursday keep-kill set the above/below line and confirmed Nov 6. Friday's session was folded into Thursday afternoon, which set the backwards plan, the four lanes and the meeting cadence.

initiatives.title: Build the customer-facing MVP
initiatives.notes: Six dev weeks from Sep 14 with three weeks of design overlapping the front, then two QA weeks. Feature freeze Friday Oct 23 — no new surfaces after that, bugs only. Above the line: renewal queue, outreach review and send, questionnaire, VA shopping of three carriers, shop results, the insured proposal page, and a needs-binding state that cannot silently disappear.

initiatives.title: Launch the MVP
initiatives.notes: Ship date — Friday Nov 6. One paying agency live, running their real renewal week on the software. Confirmed at the Sep 10 keep-kill. Definition of done is the seven above-the-line surfaces plus emails leaving the agent's own mailbox on the Tuesday 9:00 schedule, a VA kit that makes the 24-hour promise true, and an onboarding runbook someone outside the room can follow.

initiatives.title: Run the October design partner
initiatives.notes: Candidate identified in the Sep 10 session and being approached. Free shopping and VA practice — a second agency's reality before we charge anyone. Starts the week dev begins shipping user-facing surfaces and runs to launch, doubling as the QA population for the last two weeks. Then hands off and the first paying customer onboards Nov 6.

initiatives.title: Iterate the MVP with first customers
initiatives.notes: Runs in tandem with Release 2 (close the loop). Learn deep on the first logos.

initiatives.title: Close the loop (R2)
initiatives.notes: Record calls/Zooms; write fresh detail back into the repository.

initiatives.title: Build the VA portal (R3)
initiatives.notes: Internal VA queues, upload, verification. Can start lighter / internal-tool while customer product stays engineer-built.

initiatives.title: Pull the full book from AMS (R4)
initiatives.notes: Onboarding unlock — EasyLinks / HawkSoft first. Without this, manual book download caps add rate.

initiatives.title: Stand up gig-style VA onboarding (R5)
initiatives.notes: Digital training + workflow so VAs come online without heavy babysitting. First VA may become manager/trainer.

initiatives.title: Replace the AMS for data visibility (R6)
initiatives.notes: Show the repository internally, then to clients. Automated shopping deferred ~2 years (not on this near-term track).

initiatives.title: Conduct AMS research
initiatives.notes: Path 2 ops architecture drafted (Aug 7): light CSV onboard + weekly renewal report + shortlist RPA + Zapier write-back. Feasibility closed — we can launch without an AMS API.

initiatives.title: Establish Q4 OKRs
initiatives.notes: First pass drafted across the four lanes — people, capital, customers, product — then revised by the team at the first weekly on Thursday Sep 17. Becomes the format for the monthly report-out. Monday How Should We is retired; this team runs the weekly from here.

initiatives.title: Hire the first VA — senior manager
initiatives.notes: Hired in the country where we intend to build the team, treated as a core team member with a title and an exclusivity agreement — not a US W-2 employee. They build the process and hire the next ten. Davie owns the relationship; Austin runs tooling and shopping protocols as a consultant. Offer targeted the week of Sep 21. Blocked on employment agreements.

initiatives.title: Secure company insurance — cyber, data liability, workers' comp
initiatives.notes: Historically written on the studio. With employees and this data profile it needs its own liability structure now. Bundles with the workers' comp shopping that has to happen anyway.

initiatives.title: Build the investor pack
initiatives.notes: Everything ready before the Sep 28 conference: pitch deck, incorporation docs, term sheet, and a data room, so a hallway conversation can end with “can you share that with me.” Content edits on the deck due Sep 21, leaving a week for design. Still to add: investor guidance, an investor CRM, and an outreach cadence.

initiatives.title: Frame the SPV
initiatives.notes: A special purpose vehicle so the network can come in through one instrument. Only the framing is needed before the conference — the event is about soliciting interest, not closing.

initiatives.title: Secure investor commitments
initiatives.notes: Commitments for money by Oct 15. Separate from revenue — pre-selling starts before then and we launch with revenue in October.

initiatives.title: Draft customer contracts with counsel
initiatives.notes: Kicks off with a 60-minute call to lay out terms and concerns — 24-month agreement, pricing mechanics, data protections — then a session with counsel. SaaS template from the California firm; insurance-specific language coached separately. Hard constraint: a percentage of premium cannot be tied to a specific policy, cannot be named on a commission account, and the word “commission” cannot appear in the documents.

initiatives.title: Book 120 demos
initiatives.notes: The one metric that matters. Roughly 90 held at a 75% show rate. Ramp checkpoint is ~18 booked by Oct 2 — September is the fragile part, because paid cannot make up a shortfall it has not learned enough to cover.

initiatives.title: Launch paid social v1
initiatives.notes: The swing play. v1 live Sep 18 against a standalone landing page rather than waiting on website v2. The hard part is instrumentation — feeding the algorithms which videos become demos — and the ask is to have it crawling in about a month. Creative, not destination, is the likely blocker.

initiatives.title: Close ~30 contracts
initiatives.notes: Roughly a third of held demos. Execution is manual DocuSign first, built into the product later. Open: who preps, QAs, routes and files signed documents, and who owns onboarding when these land while we are stabilizing customer one.

initiatives.notes: First live design-partner pilot. Ten working sessions plus the Aug 3 retro.
